section.sectionSummaryBrief: The verse commands dwelling in sukkos for seven days, and the Rebbe introduces the connection between sukkah and peace, the four species, and the seventy bulls.
section.t: “You shall dwell in sukkos for seven days”
(and adds another command)
“every native-born Jew shall dwell in sukkos”
(and the reason for this)
“so that your generations may know that I caused the children of Israel to dwell in sukkos when I brought them out of the land of Egypt” etc.1
And the precise points in this are known from the discourses of our Nesi’im,
and prefacing with what the Baal HaHilula2 said,
that sukkah is the matter of peace, as it is written3
“and spread over us the sukkah of Your peace,”
and one must understand what is the connection of sukkah to peace.
Now, during the seven days of Sukkos there are several matters,
which are related to “you shall dwell in sukkos for seven days.”
And like the mitzvah of taking the Four Species
(“And you shall take for yourselves4
on the first day” etc.)
which has a connection to the matter of sukkah.
And as is known5
that the optimal mitzvah is that the taking of the Four Species be in the sukkah.
And also during the seven days of Sukkos there is the matter of offering seventy bulls, corresponding to the seventy nations, as brought in the Midrash6.
And this matter also exists now, as it is written “and we will render [the] bulls [of] our lips”7,
and particularly according to what is explained8
that “venashalmah” is not only the matter of completion but also from the term shleimus (perfection),
meaning that even during the time of exile,
through reciting the verses of the offerings of the seventy bulls, the matter is in its perfection,
and even though during the time of exile,
since the action is only through “our lips,”
it is not apparent openly in physicality, and certainly not in the materiality of the world,
nevertheless,
since the movement of one’s lips is considered an action9,
and as is explained at length in Tanya10,
so even now the action is in its perfection in spirituality
(and at least in a minor action).
And one must understand,
what is the connection of these matters
(taking the Four Species and offering the seventy bulls)
to the matter of sukkah.
Now, when the first day of the festival falls on Shabbat
[as in the determination of this year]
there is a difference between the time of the Temple and the time of exile
[similar to11
the sounding of the shofar on Rosh HaShanah that falls on Shabbat,
that in the Temple they would sound it but not in the provinces],
that during the time of the Temple, on the first day of the festival, the lulav overrides Shabbat even in the borderlands,
but since the destruction of the Temple, the lulav does not override Shabbat even on the first day,
as explained in the Mishnah and Gemara12.
